evidence: Enumerated every shipped criterion: 2 gate (hro_gate_render, hro_gate_shared), 40 functional, 5 polish, 5 visual likert. Each binary criterion names a concrete browser-observable end state with an explicit failure condition, and the shared protocols supply durable, distinctive evidence: (1) Probes are distinctive and absent from seed/reference: functional prompt.md:15 'Use your own new jobs and cards for every board protocol (suffix every title and name for this review)'; polish hro_pol_live_board probe 'Call back on Fri' does not occur in environment/assets/seed_data.json, solution/app/src/seed_data.json, public/index.html or public/js/*.js (grep: no hits); polish/visual prompts also mandate suffixed titles. (2) Durable evidence, not 'looks right': state is read back in an independent browser context (prompt.md:11 newContext recipe; hro_job_open, hro_add_candidate, hro_reorder, hro_notes), after restart_app (hro_restart, prompt.md:51), after reload (hro_drafts, hro_pol_failed_send note draft), and as before/after facts per row (prompt.md:19). (3) Refusals are not response-shape-only: every refusal row requires 'nothing changed' plus its own positive control (prompt.md:13 'Every refusal row needs its own positive control'; e.g. hro_interview_full 'the two cards that entered Interview are the control', hro_observer_readonly 'Rafael's identical successful requests are the control', hro_anonymous 'A signed-in success of each is the control'); where the UI hides an action, server refusal is proven by replay of a captured real request (prompt.md:17,23), so client-only enforcement cannot pass. The only status-code assertion (hro_anonymous '401') is paired with 'nothing changes' and backed by the public rule hireops_rules.md:21 'A caller with no valid session reads and writes nothing: 401'. (4) Time-varying/focus outcomes are given concrete probes: 15-second no-reload waits with an explicit snapshot rule (prompt.md:41,47; polish prompt.md:14), document.activeElement and getBoundingClientRect/scroll offsets read via page.evaluate (hro_refused_put_back, hro_pol_live_board, hro_pol_earlier_place, polish prompt.md:14), and an aborted single request or setOffline for failed send (hro_pol_failed_send). (5) Seeded expectations quoted in criteria are correct: hro_unread_counts 'Lena Fischer starts with 1 unread' matches seed (APP-301 has 3 messages, USR-CAN3 read_count 2) and protocol Z reads it first; functional is the first scored suite under rewardkit --max-concurrent-agent 1 (test.sh:207) and gates/polish/visual never touch Lena; app_context.md:30 '120 messages at the start' matches seed (APP-101: 120). Counts that later reviews can disturb are stated relatively (hro_unread_counts Mei 'computed from the observed sequence'; T fallback 'counts read relative to their values before you act'). (6) Visual rows are likert craft judgements with five described anchors on named surfaces (visual judge.toml lines 23-90; prompt.md:14 lists the surfaces); per skill check-41 guidance that is the shipped craft format, not a 'looks right' binary. Weak-app reasoning: a client-only rules app fails the replay legs; a browser-only/localStorage app fails the independent-context readbacks and the gate; a polling app that re-renders and drops focus/draft fails the polish activeElement/value probes; a no-op app that 'refuses everything' fails the paired controls. Conforming-alternative reasoning: criteria explicitly allow hiding refused controls ('hiding it is optional'), refusing before dispatch (hro_refused_put_back second sentence), any route/label (prompt.md:15), names in response or on screen (hro_stale_refused/protocol C), and sessions per tab (hro_pol_session_resume). Latent decidability notes (P3, not defects, recorded for the owner): (a) hro_job_open's replay 'with a Recruiter's account as the hiring manager' needs a recruiter identifier in observed product data; the golden exposes recruiter_id in job objects (board.js:73 sends manager_id; index.js:205 validates role), but an alternative that never exposes a recruiter id could leave that sub-leg undecidable with no stated fallback. (b) hro_candidate_private 'no response a candidate page receives contains ...' requires capturing response bodies; an open SSE stream body cannot be read by page.on('response').body() until it ends, so a leak only via a streaming channel is harder for the judge to observe (websocket frames are observable). (c) Out of row scope, for row 33: hro_activity says 'every successful action you performed on J1 and J2' while protocol A (prompt.md:49) lists only 'S, M, L, C, B and R', omitting T's Tomas card add, K's Tomas moves/reject/reopen and V's Mei move/add; both are decidable, but the two scopes differ. Risk=true because browser decidability of the heaviest legs (full candidate response inspection, full activity ledger, replays) has not been measured by a configured claude-code judge run; raw-evidence-index scope states 'Full configured grading/workload ... are absent' and workspace.json is 'Scripted golden observations; not a configured judge run'. That missing measurement is not waived by this Pass.
